objects.definition: static const int kMaxFilenameLength = 255;
objects.description: A file-scope constant defining the maximum filename length as 255. Although not a user-defined type, it is a constant integral value. Note: This header does not define a custom data type for it; included here only to acknowledge presence. No type aliases beyond the intrinsic int.

Signed 32-bit identifier type for objects/records (IdType) and its unsigned 32-bit counterpart (IdTypeUnsign). Negative IdType values denote missing/invalid IDs. Intended for datasets not exceeding 32-bit ranges; switching to 64-bit would require broader code review for alignment and usage assumptions.
Signed 32-bit label type. Negative values can represent missing labels. Constants in this header define a prefix string and an EMPTY_LABEL sentinel as the minimal 32-bit value.

objects.definition: typedef std::mt19937 RandomGeneratorType;
objects.description: Alias for the Mersenne Twister 32-bit RNG engine used for thread-local random generation within the library.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only provides a portability macro mapping __builtin_popcount to __popcnt for MSVC. There are no custom data types to document.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only provides a prefetch macro (PREFETCH) with platform-specific implementations and includes for intrinsics. There are no forward declarations or type aliases introduced here.
This header does not define any custom data types (no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes). It only includes platform-specific intrinsic headers conditionally based on target architecture macros.

objects.definition: enum LogSeverity {LIB_DEBUG, LIB_INFO, LIB_WARNING, LIB_ERROR, LIB_FATAL};
objects.description: Enumeration of log severity levels used throughout the logging system, from debug to fatal.

objects.definition: enum LogChoice  {LIB_LOGNONE, LIB_LOGFILE, LIB_LOGSTDERR, LIB_LOGCUSTOM};
objects.description: Enumeration controlling the global logger destination/selection: none, file, stderr, or a custom implementation.
Abstract base class for log backends. Implementers must override log(...) to handle a message at a given severity with file/line/function context. Destructor is virtual.
Concrete Logger that writes log messages to standard error. Provides a log(...) override; no explicit constructor is declared.
Concrete Logger that writes log messages to a specified file. Owns an ofstream member named logfile. Requires a path in its constructor.

A RAII log entry builder. Accumulates stream-formatted content via operator<< and, upon destruction, emits the message using the provided Logger with captured context. If severity is LIB_FATAL, calls exit(1) after logging.

Helper class to build a contextual runtime_error message using a stream interface. Stores a stringstream and exposes it via stream(). Constructor records file/line/function for message composition (implementation not shown).

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only defines a set of file-scope constants of type std::string, unsigned, float, double, and bool representing command-line option names, help messages, and default values.

Referenced as a shared_ptr parameter type for space/index/query parameters, but not defined in this header. Since there is no definition or forward declaration here, it should be ignored per instructions. However, noting presence: AnyParams appears to represent a generic parameter container. Details unknown.

Container for name=value parameter pairs used across the library. Stores two parallel vectors of names and string values, supports parsing from strings, comparison while ignoring specific keys, mutation, and conversion to string. It throws on bad formats and duplicates. Details about lifetime management and constraints are inferred from code; no special destruction is needed.

Parameter accessor/validator for AnyParams. Provides typed retrieval (required/optional), extraction utilities, tracking of which parameters were consumed, and validation of unknown parameters. Performs string-to-type conversion with errors on failure. No special destruction is required.

Owns or references a contiguous buffer that stores an object record: [4-byte id][4-byte label][8-byte data length][data bytes]. Provides accessors to id, label, length, and data pointer; supports cloning and optional ownership of the underlying buffer. Lifetime: if constructed with allocated memory (second ctor or CreateNewEmptyObject/Clone), it frees the buffer in destructor; if constructed with external buffer and memory_allocated=false, it will not free it.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<const Object*> ObjectVector;
objects.description: Alias for a vector of pointers to const Object, representing a collection of dataset objects. Does not own the pointed objects by itself.

objects.definition: typedef std::list<const Object*> ObjectList;
objects.description: Alias for a list of pointers to const Object, an alternative container for object pointers. Does not own the pointed objects.
Comparator functor that orders Object pointers by their id() in ascending order.

Base input-state handle for reading dataset/object data files. Provides a virtual Close and virtual destructor so derived state objects can manage file resources and per-file parsing state. Details beyond Close are unknown from this header.

Concrete input-state for a single input file. Owns an ifstream and tracks a line counter. Close closes the stream. Throws if the file cannot be opened. Used by Space implementations for text/binary ingestion.
Input-state for vector data files. Inherits file/line handling and adds a remembered dimensionality (dim_) to enforce consistency across vectors during reading.
Output-state wrapper that owns an ofstream and sets exception flags. Used by Space implementations to serialize objects/datasets and to manage output lifecycle via Close.

There are no custom structs, classes, enums, or typedefs defined in this header. The only symbols are a macro (MAX_LEVEN_BUFFER_QTY) and two templated function declarations/definitions for levenshtein; functions are not data types and are therefore excluded per instructions.

objects.definition: #define METH_DUMMY             "dummy"
objects.description: A preprocessor macro defining the method name string literal "dummy". Not a type. No standalone type definitions are provided here for string; std::string is referenced via using std::string; but not defined in this header. Note: This entry is informational; there are no new typedefs or aliases for std::string defined here.

Simple POD struct holding an identifier (id) and an associated frequency/count (qty). Used when merging/processing posting lists to keep track of how many times an id appears. Constructor defaults to id=0 and qty=0.

objects.definition: typedef vector<IdCount> VectIdCount;
objects.description: Type alias for a std::vector of IdCount entries, representing a multiset/posting list with counts for each id.

objects.definition: typedef vector<IdTypeUnsign> PostingListInt;
objects.description: Type alias for a std::vector of IdTypeUnsign representing a posting list of raw unsigned ids without counts. IdTypeUnsign is declared elsewhere (in idtype.h).

Graph node used in the Small World randomized graph index. Wraps an Object pointer, stores an internal Id, and maintains a sorted adjacency list of neighbor MSWNode pointers ("friends"). Provides thread-safe friend insertion and utilities to remove or patch neighbors during deletions. Requires external ownership of Object; mutex accessGuard_ must be respected during indexing when accessing friends_.

SIFT-specialized metric space implementing squared L2 distance for 128-D SIFT descriptors. Provides object I/O from strings/files, creation from uint8 vectors, dense vector extraction, approximate equality, and computes distances via a precomputed AVX-optimized routine. Inherits from Space<DistTypeSIFT>. Some details (e.g., SIFT_DIM, DistTypeSIFT, Object types) are defined elsewhere.

Concrete string-space class computing plain Levenshtein edit distance between two objects' character data. Inherits from StringSpace<int>. HiddenDistance converts stored object payloads to char buffers and returns levenshtein(x,len1,y,len2). Copy/assignment is disabled via DISABLE_COPY_AND_ASSIGN. Construction/destruction have no special behavior beyond defaults.

Concrete string-space class computing normalized Levenshtein distance (edit distance divided by max(len1,len2)). Inherits from StringSpace<float>. Treats both-empty strings as distance 0; otherwise asserts at least one non-empty. Copy/assignment disabled.

Concrete space class that fuses sparse and dense components for distance computation. It derives from Space<float> and provides dataset I/O hooks, proxy/hidden distance evaluation, and composition via CompDesc descriptors and per-role weights loaded from a weight file. Many serialization methods are intentionally unimplemented in this header. Details of CompDesc and DataFile* types are defined elsewhere.

Concrete Space implementation in the similarity namespace that handles sparse vectors in a binary on-disk format using cosine similarity. It derives from SpaceSparseCosineSimilarityFast (defined elsewhere) and overrides file I/O and object creation to support the binary fast format. It is non-copyable per DISABLE_COPY_AND_ASSIGN.

Concrete Space implementation in the similarity namespace for sparse vectors stored in a fast binary format using negative scalar product (i.e., -dot product) as the distance. Inherits from SpaceSparseNegativeScalarProductFast (defined elsewhere). Provides overrides for reading headers, reading objects, and constructing objects from strings. Non-copyable via DISABLE_COPY_AND_ASSIGN.

Base pivot-index class specialized for sparse-vector dot-product based distances. It builds an in-memory inverted index over pivot elements and can compute pivot distances both at index time and query time. Supports optional L2 normalization of data and/or queries and optional dimensionality reduction via a hashing trick. Construction triggers index building via createIndex().

Space implementing cosine similarity over sparse vectors with a fast computation path. Provides a pivot index that normalizes both data and queries, computes dot products, and converts them to cosine distance 1 - cos, clamped at 0. HiddenDistance returns the cosine distance between two objects.

Space implementing angular distance over sparse vectors. Uses a pivot index that normalizes vectors and converts normalized dot products to angular distance via acos. HiddenDistance computes the angular distance between two objects.

Space implementing the negative scalar product distance over sparse vectors. Its pivot index does not normalize data or queries and negates dot-product results to serve as distances. HiddenDistance returns the negative dot product between two objects.

Space computing negative scalar product where only the query vectors are normalized. The pivot index normalizes queries but not data and negates dot-product results for use as distances. HiddenDistance applies this asymmetric normalization scheme.

Holds statistics about the overlap between two sparse vectors: count of shared dimensions, normalized dot product over the overlap, and per-side overlap/difference sums, means, and standard deviations. Useful for cosine-related analyses and intersection-based computations.

functions.name: similarity::GetFileName
functions.signature: const char* similarity::GetFileName(const char* fullpath)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the filename component of a path. Likely strips directory components from a full path. Definition is not present in this header; behavior regarding returned pointer lifetime and handling of trailing separators is unknown.
requirements: fullpath must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer (non-null).
Returned pointer likely aliases memory within fullpath; do not free it. Exact ownership/lifetime semantics are unknown due to missing definition.

functions.name: similarity::CreateDir
functions.signature: bool similarity::CreateDir(const char* name, int mode = 0777)
functions.description: Creates a directory with the given name and permissions. Returns true on success and false on failure. Implementation is not shown here; typical behavior is to attempt creation if it does not exist.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer (non-null).
mode specifies permission bits; interpretation is platform-dependent (default 0777).
May fail if the directory already exists or permissions are insufficient; caller should check the boolean return.

functions.name: similarity::DoesFileExist
functions.signature: bool similarity::DoesFileExist(const char* filename)
functions.description: Checks whether a file exists at the given path. Returns true if it exists, false otherwise. This is the base overload used by the string wrapper.
requirements: filename must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer (non-null).
Caller must check the boolean return value to branch on existence.

functions.name: similarity::getThreadLocalRandomGenerator
functions.signature: inline similarity::RandomGeneratorType& similarity::getThreadLocalRandomGenerator()
functions.description: Returns a thread-local Mersenne Twister (std::mt19937) random number generator reference, initialized with the global defaultRandomSeed. Safe to call from multiple threads; each thread gets its own generator instance.
requirements: defaultRandomSeed (extern int) should be initialized before use to control seeding; otherwise it defaults to zero-initialized static storage per C++ rules.
Do not store the reference across thread termination; only use within the same thread.

functions.name: similarity::RandomInt
functions.signature: inline int32_t similarity::RandomInt()
functions.description: Generates a thread-safe pseudo-random 32-bit integer uniformly distributed in [0, std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max()]. Uses a thread-local generator.
requirements: No arguments. Thread-safe as long as each thread uses its own generator via the thread-local facility.
Caller should not assume cryptographic randomness.

functions.name: similarity::RandomReal
functions.signature: template <class T> inline T similarity::RandomReal()
functions.description: Generates a thread-safe pseudo-random real number uniformly distributed in [0, 1). Uses std::uniform_real_distribution<T> on a thread-local generator.
requirements: T must be a floating-point type supported by std::uniform_real_distribution (e.g., float, double, long double).
Caller should not assume cryptographic randomness.

functions.name: similarity::RStrip
functions.signature: void similarity::RStrip(char* str)
functions.description: Removes trailing whitespace characters from a C-string in place (right-strip). Definition not included here; typical behavior is to trim spaces, tabs, and other isspace() characters from the end.
requirements: str must be a valid, mutable, null-terminated C string pointer (non-null).
The buffer must be writable; function modifies the string in place.

functions.name: similarity::Mean
functions.signature: template <typename dist_t> dist_t similarity::Mean(const dist_t* array, const unsigned size)
functions.description: Computes the arithmetic mean of an array of values. Returns 0 if size == 0.
requirements: array must point to at least size elements; must be non-null if size > 0.
dist_t must support addition, division by unsigned, and default construction from 0 literal.
If size == 0, the function returns 0 (which may be 0 or 0.0 depending on dist_t).

functions.name: similarity::Sum
functions.signature: template <typename dist_t> dist_t similarity::Sum(const dist_t* array, const unsigned size)
functions.description: Computes the sum of an array of values and returns it.
requirements: array must point to at least size elements; must be non-null if size > 0.
dist_t must support addition and default construction from 0 literal.

functions.name: similarity::Variance
functions.signature: template <typename dist_t> dist_t similarity::Variance(const dist_t* array, const unsigned size, const dist_t mean)
functions.description: Computes the unbiased sample variance given precomputed mean. If size >= 2, returns sum((x - mean)^2)/(size-1); otherwise returns 0.
requirements: array must point to at least size elements; must be non-null if size > 0.
size should be >= 2 to obtain a meaningful (unbiased) variance; for size < 2, the function returns 0.
dist_t must support subtraction, multiplication, addition, and division by an unsigned.

functions.name: similarity::StdDev
functions.signature: template <typename dist_t> dist_t similarity::StdDev(const dist_t* array, const unsigned size)
functions.description: Computes the standard deviation as sqrt(Variance(array, size)).
requirements: array must point to at least size elements; must be non-null if size > 0.
dist_t must be usable with sqrt (i.e., convertibly callable with std::sqrt) and support required arithmetic.

functions.name: similarity::DistMax
functions.signature: template <typename dist_t> inline dist_t similarity::DistMax()
functions.description: Returns half of the maximum representable value for dist_t, i.e., numeric_limits<dist_t>::max() / 2. Intended to avoid overflow in integer distance types.
requirements: dist_t must be a numeric type supported by std::numeric_limits.

functions.name: similarity::ApproxEqual
functions.signature: template <typename T> bool similarity::ApproxEqual(const T& x, const T& y, unsigned maxUlps = MAX_ULPS)
functions.description: Tests approximate equality of two values. Comments indicate for floating-point it compares within maxUlps (default 4 ULPs) or near 2*epsilon; for integral types approximate equality degenerates to exact equality. Definition is not present in this header.
requirements: T should be arithmetic (floating-point or integral) compatible with an ULP-based comparison.
maxUlps controls tolerance; default is MAX_ULPS (4). Exact comparison rules are inferred and may vary since definition is missing.

functions.name: similarity::round1
functions.signature: inline double similarity::round1(double x)
functions.description: Rounds x to one decimal place using std::round(x*10.0)/10.0.
requirements: Input x is any finite double; behavior follows std::round for infinities/NaN.

functions.name: similarity::round2
functions.signature: inline double similarity::round2(double x)
functions.description: Rounds x to two decimal places using std::round(x*100.0)/100.0.
requirements: Input x is any finite double; behavior follows std::round for infinities/NaN.

functions.name: similarity::round3
functions.signature: inline double similarity::round3(double x)
functions.description: Rounds x to three decimal places using std::round(x*1000.0)/1000.0.
requirements: Input x is any finite double; behavior follows std::round for infinities/NaN.

functions.name: similarity::SplitStr
functions.signature: template <typename ElemType> inline bool similarity::SplitStr(const std::string& str_, std::vector<ElemType>& res, const char SplitChar)
functions.description: Splits a string by replacing SplitChar with a space and then extracting tokens via stream extraction (operator>>). Tokens are parsed into ElemType. Returns true on success; false if a token cannot be parsed. Clears res before filling.
requirements: str_ should not contain whitespace within intended tokens; stream extraction splits on whitespace.
Tokens cannot contain the SplitChar (it is treated as a separator) and cannot contain spaces; escaping is not supported.
ElemType must be stream-extractable via operator>>(std::istream&, ElemType&).
On failure to parse a token, the function returns false and res may contain a partial result.

functions.name: similarity::MergeIntoStr
functions.signature: template <typename ElemType> inline std::string similarity::MergeIntoStr(const std::vector<ElemType>& ve, char MergeChar)
functions.description: Joins elements of a vector into a single string, inserting MergeChar between elements. Elements are formatted using stream insertion (operator<<).
requirements: ElemType must be stream-insertable via operator<<(std::ostream&, const ElemType&).

functions.name: similarity::ConvertToString
functions.signature: template <typename obj_type> inline std::string similarity::ConvertToString(const obj_type& o)
functions.description: Converts an object to its string representation using stream insertion into a stringstream.
requirements: obj_type must be stream-insertable via operator<<(std::ostream&, const obj_type&).

functions.name: similarity::ConvertFromString
functions.signature: template <typename obj_type> inline void similarity::ConvertFromString(const std::string& s, obj_type& o)
functions.description: Parses a string into an object via stream extraction. Throws std::runtime_error if parsing fails or extra characters remain after parsing.
requirements: obj_type must be stream-extractable via operator>>(std::istream&, obj_type&).
s must contain a representation of exactly one object with no trailing non-whitespace characters; otherwise a runtime_error is thrown.
Caller must handle exceptions on failure.

functions.name: similarity::ReadField
functions.signature: template <typename FieldType> inline void similarity::ReadField(std::istream& in, const std::string& fieldName, FieldType& fieldValue)
functions.description: Reads a single line from input in the format "fieldName:fieldValue", verifies the field name matches, and converts the value to FieldType using ConvertFromString. Throws std::runtime_error on errors (I/O error, empty line, missing delimiter, name mismatch, or conversion failure).
requirements: Input stream in must be readable; a full line must be available.
The line must contain the FIELD_DELIMITER ':' character.
The field name before ':' must exactly equal fieldName.
FieldType must be supported by ConvertFromString (i.e., stream-extractable or have a specialization).
Caller must handle exceptions on failure.

functions.name: similarity::WriteField
functions.signature: template <typename FieldType> inline void similarity::WriteField(std::ostream& out, const std::string& fieldName, const FieldType& fieldValue)
functions.description: Writes a line "fieldName:fieldValue\n" to the output stream using stream insertion. Throws std::runtime_error if writing fails.
requirements: Output stream out must be writable; failures will throw.
FieldType must be stream-insertable via operator<<.
Caller must handle exceptions on failure.

functions.name: similarity::writeBinaryPOD
functions.signature: template <typename T> void similarity::writeBinaryPOD(std::ostream& out, const T& podRef)
functions.description: Writes a Plain Old Data (POD) value to a std::ostream as raw bytes using out.write. Does not perform endianness conversion.
requirements: out should be opened in binary mode to avoid data transformation on some platforms.
T must be trivially copyable/POD-compatible for meaningful binary serialization.
Exactly sizeof(T) bytes are written; caller should ensure the stream is positioned appropriately and check stream state if needed.

functions.name: similarity::readBinaryPOD
functions.signature: template <typename T> static void similarity::readBinaryPOD(std::istream& in, T& podRef)
functions.description: Reads sizeof(T) bytes from a std::istream into podRef using in.read. Does not perform endianness conversion.
requirements: in should be opened in binary mode to avoid translation.
T must be trivially copyable/POD-compatible for meaningful binary deserialization.
Exactly sizeof(T) bytes are attempted; caller should verify stream state after the call.

functions.name: similarity::ToLower
functions.signature: inline void similarity::ToLower(std::string& s)
functions.description: Converts all characters in the string to lowercase in place using std::tolower on each char.
requirements: s is modified in place; caller must provide a mutable string.
Behavior of std::tolower can be affected by current locale.

functions.name: similarity::StartsWith
functions.signature: inline bool similarity::StartsWith(const std::string& str, const std::string& prefix)
functions.description: Returns true if str begins with prefix, false otherwise.
requirements: No special requirements; operates on any strings.
Complexity is proportional to prefix length.

functions.name: similarity::HasWhiteSpace
functions.signature: inline bool similarity::HasWhiteSpace(const std::string& s)
functions.description: Returns true if any character in the string is whitespace according to std::isspace, otherwise false.
requirements: Behavior of std::isspace can be affected by current locale.

functions.name: similarity::ReplaceSomePunct
functions.signature: inline void similarity::ReplaceSomePunct(std::string& s)
functions.description: Replaces commas ',' and the FIELD_DELIMITER ':' with spaces in the string, leaving periods intact.
requirements: s is modified in place.

functions.name: similarity::getRelDiff
functions.signature: template <class T> T similarity::getRelDiff(T val1, T val2)
functions.description: Computes the relative difference |val1 - val2| / max(max(|val1|, |val2|), numeric_limits<T>::min()). Helps avoid division by zero for very small magnitudes.
requirements: T must support std::fabs, std::max, subtraction, division, and have numeric_limits specialization.
Intended for floating-point T; using integral T may cause unintended implicit conversions.

functions.name: FloatingPointDiff::AlmostEquals
functions.signature:
template <typename RawType>
bool FloatingPointDiff<RawType>::AlmostEquals(const FloatingPointDiff<RawType>& rhs, size_t maxUlps) const
functions.description: Compares two FloatingPointDiff<RawType> values for near-equality by checking whether their distance in ULPs is within a caller-specified bound. Returns false if either operand is NaN; otherwise true when ULP difference <= maxUlps. Intended for tolerant float/double comparisons in tests or numeric code.
requirements: This method must be called on a valid, initialized FloatingPointDiff<RawType> instance.
The rhs object must be the same template instantiation (i.e., FloatingPointDiff<RawType>).
maxUlps is a size_t (non-negative by type) that defines the maximum allowed ULP distance.
If either wrapped value is NaN, the comparison will return false (behavior by design).
RawType must be a 32-bit or 64-bit IEEE-754-like floating-point type; otherwise the internal Bits alias will be ill-formed (TypeWithSize has specializations only for 4 and 8).

functions.name: FloatingPointDiff::ULP_diff
functions.signature:
template <typename RawType>
typename FloatingPointDiff<RawType>::Bits FloatingPointDiff<RawType>::ULP_diff(const FloatingPointDiff<RawType>& rhs) const
functions.description: Computes and returns the distance between two floating-point values in units in the last place (ULPs). This overload takes another FloatingPointDiff<RawType> and returns the absolute ULP difference as an unsigned integer of the underlying bit-width.
requirements: This method must be called on a valid, initialized FloatingPointDiff<RawType> instance.
The rhs object must be the same template instantiation (i.e., FloatingPointDiff<RawType>).
The returned value is an absolute ULP distance in the typedef Bits (32 or 64-bit unsigned).
RawType must be a 32-bit or 64-bit IEEE-754-like floating-point type; otherwise the internal Bits alias will be ill-formed.

functions.name: FloatingPointDiff::is_nan
functions.signature:
template <typename RawType>
bool FloatingPointDiff<RawType>::is_nan() const
functions.description: Returns true if the wrapped value is a NaN (exponent all ones and a non-zero fraction), false otherwise. Implements a bitwise IEEE-754 NaN check for the RawType.
requirements: This method must be called on a valid, initialized FloatingPointDiff<RawType> instance.
RawType must be a 32-bit or 64-bit IEEE-754-like floating-point type to match the bit-mask logic used.

functions.name: LibGetCurrentTime
functions.signature: std::string LibGetCurrentTime();
functions.description: Returns the current time as a string. Intended for timestamping log messages. Exact format is not specified in this header.
requirements: No arguments.
Return value format is unknown; callers should not assume a specific format.

functions.name: InitializeLogger
functions.signature: void InitializeLogger(LogChoice choice = LIB_LOGNONE, const char* logfile = NULL);
functions.description: Initializes the global logger to the specified logging destination. Supports none, file, stderr, or a custom logger mode per LogChoice. When configured, subsequent LOG/ DLOG macros will use the global logger.
requirements: If choice is LIB_LOGFILE, logfile should point to a valid path string; behavior for NULL or invalid paths is not specified.
If choice is LIB_LOGSTDERR, logfile is ignored.
If choice is LIB_LOGNONE, logging is effectively disabled.
If choice is LIB_LOGCUSTOM, behavior is unknown from this header (likely requires setGlobalLogger to be called separately).
Should be called before emitting logs via LOG/DLOG to ensure a logger is available; otherwise logging may be skipped (getGlobalLogger can be NULL).
Thread-safety is unspecified.

functions.name: Logger::~Logger
functions.signature: virtual ~Logger();
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the Logger abstract base class, enabling proper cleanup via base-class pointers.
requirements: Derived loggers should ensure any resources are released in their destructors.
Objects deleted through a Logger* must have a virtual destructor (provided here).

functions.name: Logger::log
functions.signature: virtual void log(LogSeverity severity, const char * file, int line, const char * function, const std::string & message) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual method to emit a log record. Implementations define how/where the log is written (e.g., stderr, file).
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
severity is one of {LIB_DEBUG, LIB_INFO, LIB_WARNING, LIB_ERROR, LIB_FATAL}.
file and function are C-strings typically coming from __FILE__/__FUNCTION__; may be NULL or non-null—this header does not specify; implementations should handle them robustly.
line is the source line number associated with the log site.
message contains the formatted log text; implementations should not modify it.
Thread-safety expectations are not specified.

functions.name: setGlobalLogger
functions.signature: void setGlobalLogger(Logger * logger);
functions.description: Sets the process-wide global logger used by LOG/DLOG macros and LogItem. Passing NULL disables logging (LogItem checks the pointer before invoking log).
requirements: logger may be NULL to disable logging.
If non-NULL, the Logger object must remain valid for the duration of its use by logging calls (no use-after-free).
Not guaranteed to be thread-safe; concurrent updates or reads are unspecified.

functions.name: getGlobalLogger
functions.signature: Logger * getGlobalLogger();
functions.description: Returns the current global logger pointer used by LOG/DLOG macros. May be NULL if logging is disabled or not initialized.
requirements: Callers must handle a NULL return (LogItem already checks for NULL internally).
Returned pointer is non-owning; do not delete via this pointer unless you own the logger and have ensured no further use.

functions.name: StdErrLogger::log
functions.signature: void log(LogSeverity severity, const char * file, int line, const char * function, const std::string & message);
functions.description: Emits a log record to standard error. Overrides Logger::log.
requirements: No explicit constraints beyond Logger::log parameters.
Assumes stderr is available; behavior if closed or redirected is unspecified.
Thread-safety is unspecified.

functions.name: FileLogger::FileLogger
functions.signature: FileLogger(const char * logfile);
functions.description: Constructs a logger that writes log records to the specified file.
requirements: logfile should be a non-NULL C-string path to the target log file.
The path should be writable and accessible; error handling on failure to open is unknown from this header.
Object must remain alive while used as the global logger.

functions.name: FileLogger::log
functions.signature: void log(LogSeverity severity, const char * file, int line, const char * function, const std::string & message);
functions.description: Writes a log record to the file associated with this FileLogger instance. Overrides Logger::log.
requirements: The FileLogger instance must have been successfully constructed (file opened).
No further constraints beyond Logger::log parameters.
Thread-safety and flush behavior are unspecified.

functions.name: RuntimeErrorWrapper::RuntimeErrorWrapper
functions.signature: RuntimeErrorWrapper(const std::string& file, int line, const char* function);
functions.description: Constructs a helper used to build rich runtime_error messages, typically via the PREPARE_RUNTIME_ERR/THROW_RUNTIME_ERR macros. Captures source context (file, line, function) and accumulates a message in an internal stringstream.
requirements: file is a reference to a std::string representing the source file; must remain valid during construction (copied or referenced semantics are unknown from header).
function is a C-string; no explicit lifetime requirements stated beyond call scope.
No throwing/exception behavior is specified beyond normal construction.

functions.name: RuntimeErrorWrapper::stream
functions.signature: stringstream& stream();
functions.description: Returns a reference to the internal stringstream used to build an error message. Typically used to append details before throwing with THROW_RUNTIME_ERR.
requirements: The returned reference must not be used after the RuntimeErrorWrapper object is destroyed.

functions.name: similarity::ParseCommandLine

functions.name: similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>::Instance
functions.signature: static similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>& similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>::Instance()
functions.description: Returns a singleton instance of the template registry that maps space type names to factory functions for Space<dist_t>. Typical usage: obtain the registry and then call Register to add creators or CreateSpace to instantiate a Space for a given key. Implemented with a function-local static for thread-safe (C++11 and later) initialization.
requirements: None beyond standard C++ invocation; returns a valid singleton reference that remains alive for the program lifetime.

functions.name: similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>::Register
functions.signature: void similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>::Register(const string& SpaceType, CreateFuncPtr func)
functions.description: Registers a creator function for a given space type name in the registry for the specific dist_t. The creator must construct a Space<dist_t>* from AnyParams. Subsequent calls with the same SpaceType overwrite the previous creator.
requirements: SpaceType must identify the space type to be created; using an empty or duplicate key will overwrite any existing registration for that key.
func must be a valid (non-null) function pointer compatible with Space<dist_t>* (*)(const AnyParams&).
Registration must occur before calling CreateSpace for the same SpaceType.
The registered creator must return a Space<dist_t>* appropriate for the dist_t of this registry.

functions.name: similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>::CreateSpace
functions.signature: similarity::Space<dist_t>* similarity::SpaceFactoryRegistry<dist_t>::CreateSpace(const string& SpaceType, const AnyParams& SpaceParams)
functions.description: Creates and returns a new Space<dist_t> instance by looking up the registered creator for SpaceType and invoking it with SpaceParams. If no creator is registered for SpaceType in this dist_t registry, the function throws a runtime error.
requirements: SpaceType must have been previously registered via Register for this dist_t; otherwise this function throws a runtime error.
Caller must be prepared to handle a thrown runtime error when SpaceType is not registered.
SpaceParams must satisfy the parameter requirements of the specific registered creator; invalid parameters will cause failures inside the creator (details depend on the creator).
On success, the returned pointer is owned by the caller, who is responsible for managing its lifetime (e.g., deleting it), unless otherwise documented by the specific creator.

functions.name: similarity::MethodFactoryRegistry::Instance
functions.signature: static similarity::MethodFactoryRegistry<dist_t>& Instance()
functions.description: Returns the singleton registry instance for a specific distance type (dist_t). Use this to register method creators or to construct methods via the factory for that dist_t. Typical usage: auto& reg = similarity::MethodFactoryRegistry<MyDist>::Instance();
requirements: Function is a static singleton accessor; returns a reference that remains valid for the lifetime of the program.

Thread-safety: initialization of the singleton (C++11 and later) is thread-safe, but subsequent calls to Register/CreateMethod on the returned object are not synchronized; callers must provide external synchronization if used concurrently.

functions.name: similarity::MethodFactoryRegistry::Register
functions.signature: void Register(const std::string& MethodName, similarity::Index<dist_t>* (*func)(bool, const std::string&, similarity::Space<dist_t>&, const similarity::ObjectVector&))
functions.description: Registers a creator function under MethodName for the given distance type. The registered function is later invoked by CreateMethod to construct an Index<dist_t> from the provided space and data objects. It logs the registration with the distance type name.
requirements: Must be called on similarity::MethodFactoryRegistry<dist_t> corresponding to the intended dist_t.
func must not be null and must match the exact signature: Index<dist_t>* (bool PrintProgress, const std::string& SpaceType, Space<dist_t>& space, const ObjectVector& DataObjects).
If MethodName already exists, this call overwrites the previous registration for that name (no warning beyond the log); callers should avoid unintended overwrites.
Not thread-safe; concurrent Register or CreateMethod calls require external synchronization.
MethodName content/format is not validated by this function (no explicit restrictions stated).

functions.name: similarity::MethodFactoryRegistry::CreateMethod
functions.signature: similarity::Index<dist_t>* CreateMethod(bool PrintProgress, const std::string& MethName, const std::string& SpaceType, similarity::Space<dist_t>& space, const similarity::ObjectVector& DataObjects)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a new Index<dist_t> instance by looking up a previously registered creator under MethName and invoking it with the provided parameters. If no creator is registered for MethName and dist_t, this function throws a runtime error indicating the method is not defined for the distance type.
requirements: MethName must have been registered earlier (for the same dist_t) via Register; otherwise a runtime error is thrown.
space must be a valid similarity::Space<dist_t> instance compatible with dist_t; it is passed by reference to the creator.
DataObjects must be a valid collection of objects appropriate for the provided space; it is passed as a const reference to the creator.
The returned pointer may be null if the creator returns null; callers should check for null before use.
Exceptions: throws a runtime error if MethName is not found in the registry for the given dist_t.
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls require external synchronization.
SpaceType is forwarded to the creator; no validation is performed here (semantics depend on the specific creator).
The lifetime/ownership of the returned Index<dist_t>* is managed by the caller unless otherwise documented by the specific creator implementation.

functions.name: similarity::levenshtein
functions.signature:
template <class T>
int similarity::levenshtein(const T* p1, size_t len1, const T* p2, size_t len2);
functions.description: Computes the Levenshtein (edit) distance between two sequences given by a pointer and an explicit length for each sequence. Intended for character-like or element-wise comparable sequences. Returns the minimal number of single-element insertions, deletions, and substitutions required to transform one sequence into the other. Notes: the implementation uses a stack buffer up to MAX_LEVEN_BUFFER_QTY elements; very large inputs may cause additional allocations or higher stack usage. The distance is non-negative and bounded by max(len1, len2).
requirements: p1 must point to a readable contiguous array of at least len1 elements of type T (may be null if len1 == 0).
p2 must point to a readable contiguous array of at least len2 elements of type T (may be null if len2 == 0).
Elements of type T must be comparable for equality (the algorithm compares elements to detect matches/substitutions).
len1 and len2 must accurately describe the number of readable elements at p1 and p2 respectively (no out-of-bounds access).
For a precise return without overflow, max(len1, len2) should be <= INT_MAX, since the function returns int.
This function performs no explicit error reporting; callers should treat the return value as the edit distance (>= 0).

functions.name: similarity::levenshtein
functions.signature:
template <class T>
int similarity::levenshtein(const T& s1, const T& s2);
functions.description: Convenience overload computing the Levenshtein (edit) distance between two string-like objects by forwarding to the pointer/length overload using s1.c_str(), s1.size(), s2.c_str(), s2.size(). Suitable for types similar to std::basic_string that expose c_str() and size(). Returns the minimal number of single-element insertions, deletions, and substitutions required to transform s1 into s2.
requirements: T must provide the methods c_str() and size(), where c_str() yields a pointer to a contiguous readable array of elements compatible with equality comparison and size() returns the number of elements.
The memory returned by s1.c_str() and s2.c_str() must remain valid for the duration of the call (true for typical string types).
Elements must be comparable for equality (used by the algorithm).
For a precise return without overflow, max(s1.size(), s2.size()) should be <= INT_MAX, since the function returns int.
This function performs no explicit error reporting; callers should treat the return value as the edit distance (>= 0).

functions.name: similarity::EfficientPow
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline T similarity::EfficientPow(T Base, unsigned Exp);
functions.description: Computes Base raised to a non-negative integer power Exp using an optimized sequence of multiplications. Intended as a faster alternative to std::pow for integer exponents. Use when Exp is an unsigned integer and T supports repeated multiplication without overflow/NaN behavior. Returns 1 when Exp == 0.
requirements: Exp must be a non-negative integer (type unsigned).
Type T must support multiplication (operator*) and assignment (operator=).
Inputs should be chosen so that repeated multiplication does not overflow or produce invalid values for T.
No side effects or global state are used; the function is pure.

functions.name: similarity::EfficientFractPowUtil
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline T similarity::EfficientFractPowUtil(T Base, uint64_t Exp, uint64_t MaxK);
functions.description: Computes Base raised to a fractional exponent represented in fixed-point form: the effective exponent is Exp / MaxK, where MaxK is expected to be a power of two. It iteratively takes square roots of Base and multiplies selected factors to reconstruct Base^(Exp/MaxK). Use when you already have Exp and MaxK (with MaxK a power of two).
requirements: MaxK must be a power of two and greater than 0 (the algorithm shifts and masks assuming power-of-two).
Exp must satisfy 0 <= Exp <= MaxK; otherwise the result is undefined by the algorithm’s masking/loop termination.
Base should be non-negative for real-valued results because sqrt(Base) is applied repeatedly.
Type T must be compatible with std::sqrt(T) (or sqrt found via ADL) and support multiplication (operator*), assignment, and initialization from 1 literal.
Choose Base and parameters to avoid overflow/underflow across repeated sqrt and multiplication operations.

functions.name: similarity::EfficientFractPow
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline T similarity::EfficientFractPow(T Base, T FractExp, unsigned NumDig);
functions.description: Computes Base raised to a fractional exponent FractExp in [0, 1] using up to NumDig binary digits of precision. Internally maps FractExp to Exp/MaxK with MaxK = 1 << NumDig and calls EfficientFractPowUtil. Faster than std::pow for supported cases; uses iterative square roots and multiplications.
requirements: A runtime check enforces FractExp <= 1 and NumDig != 0; callers should also ensure FractExp >= 0 (fractional exponent) as implied by the function’s purpose.
NumDig must be a positive integer; larger values increase precision (MaxK = 1 << NumDig).
Base should be non-negative for real-valued results because sqrt(Base) is applied in the underlying algorithm.
Type T must be compatible with std::ceil and basic arithmetic, and with sqrt/multiplication used by EfficientFractPowUtil.
Be aware of rounding: Exp is computed as ceil(FractExp * MaxK), which slightly biases upward.
Inputs should avoid overflow/underflow across sqrt and multiplication steps.

functions.name: similarity::PowerProxyObject::pow
functions.signature:
template <class T>
inline T similarity::PowerProxyObject<T>::pow(T base);
functions.description: Evaluates base raised to the exponent provided at PowerProxyObject construction. If the exponent can be represented as an integer-plus-fraction with at most maxDig binary fractional bits (detected during construction), computes the result efficiently via EfficientPow and EfficientFractPowUtil; otherwise falls back to std::pow(base, pOrig_). Intended for repeated pow calls with the same exponent but varying base.
requirements: The PowerProxyObject<T> must have been constructed with the desired exponent p and maxDig (documentation suggests maxDig <= 31).
The method expects base to be non-negative (comment in code).
If the stored exponent is negative, the implementation computes 1/base first; therefore base must be non-zero in this case to avoid division by zero.
Type T must support multiplication, division, comparison, and be compatible with std::pow, std::fabs, std::floor, and std::numeric_limits<T>::min used in the optimization decision.
For the optimized path, base should be non-negative due to use of EfficientFractPowUtil which applies sqrt; otherwise results may be invalid.
Callers should ensure values do not overflow/underflow during repeated multiplication/sqrt steps in the optimized path.

functions.name: SortArrBI::resize

void SortArrBI<KeyType, DataType>::resize(size_t max_elem)
functions.description: Resizes the internal storage capacity to max_elem. May invalidate references/iterators previously obtained from get_data(). Does not change the current logical size (num_elems_) except that it may cap available capacity.
requirements: Callers must not rely on previously obtained references/iterators from get_data() after calling resize; reacquire them.

If max_elem < current size() (num_elems_), behavior of stored logical elements is not explicitly defined by this header; resizing the vector may drop capacity but keeps existing elements up to the new size. Ensure max_elem >= size() to avoid truncation.

functions.name: SortArrBI::push_unsorted_grow

void SortArrBI<KeyType, DataType>::sort()
functions.description: Sorts the first size() elements of the internal array in ascending order by key using std::sort. Useful after bulk unsorted pushes.
requirements: Relies on Item::operator< which compares by key; KeyType must be less-than comparable.

functions.description: Swaps two elements at indices x and y in the internal storage using std::swap. Can be used to manipulate items but may break sorted invariants if applied within the active range.
requirements: x and y must be less than the current capacity v_.size(); no bounds checking is performed.

functions.name: SortArrBI::push_or_replace_non_empty
functions.signature:
template <typename KeyType, typename DataType>
size_t SortArrBI<KeyType, DataType>::push_or_replace_non_empty(const KeyType& key, const DataType& data)
functions.description: Inserts a new Item with key and data into the sorted prefix [0, size()) while maintaining ascending order if the container is non-empty. If key is not smaller than the last element’s key and capacity is full, insertion is skipped. Otherwise, it finds the insertion point and shifts elements via memmove, optionally increasing size by one if capacity permits. Returns the insertion index; if no insertion occurs due to full capacity and key >= last key, returns size().
requirements: The container must be non-empty: size() > 0 (assumed by the function).
The first size() elements must already be sorted ascending by key.
Item must be safely movable via memmove; specifically, Item (and thus KeyType and DataType) should be trivially copyable/memmove-safe due to raw memmove on the underlying storage.
If capacity (v_.size()) equals size() and key >= last key, no insertion occurs and size() remains unchanged.
No duplicate checking is performed; callers must handle duplicate keys/data if needed.

functions.name: SortArrBI::merge_with_sorted_items
functions.signature:
template <typename KeyType, typename DataType>
size_t SortArrBI<KeyType, DataType>::merge_with_sorted_items(Item* items, size_t item_qty)
functions.description: Merges an external array of item_qty sorted Items into the current sorted prefix [0, size()) in-place. If there is sufficient free capacity, it appends and inplace-merges; otherwise, it replaces a suffix of current elements to fill the buffer and inplace-merges. Returns the index of the first element whose used flag is false after the merge (or size() if all are marked used).
requirements: The first size() elements in this container must be sorted ascending by key.
The input array items must contain at least item_qty valid Items and must itself be sorted ascending by key.
items must be a valid, non-null pointer when item_qty > 0.
If item_qty > v_.size(), only the first v_.size() items are considered (item_qty is truncated).
Merging uses memcpy on Item elements; Item (and thus KeyType and DataType) must be trivially copyable/memcpy-safe.
Relies on std::inplace_merge; Item must be MoveAssignable/MoveInsertable as required by standard algorithms.
The semantics of the returned index depend on Item.used flags; callers must manage/interpret used flags appropriately. If no elements have used==false, the function returns size().

functions.signature:

size_t SortArrBI<KeyType, DataType>::push_or_replace_non_empty_exp(const KeyType& key, const DataType& data)
functions.description: Like push_or_replace_non_empty but uses exponential search followed by lower_bound to locate the insertion point in a sorted prefix [0, size()). If capacity allows, increases size and inserts the new item by shifting elements via memmove; otherwise may skip insertion if key >= last key and at full capacity. Returns the insertion index, or size() if no insertion occurs in the early-out case.
requirements: The container must be non-empty: size() > 0.
The first size() elements must be sorted ascending by key.
Item must be safely movable via memmove; Item (and underlying KeyType and DataType) should be trivially copyable/memmove-safe.
No duplicate checking is performed; callers must handle duplicates if needed.

functions.name: similarity::HnswNode::getNeighborsByHeuristic1
functions.signature:
template <typename dist_t>
void similarity::HnswNode::getNeighborsByHeuristic1(std::priority_queue<similarity::HnswNodeDistCloser<dist_t>>& resultSet1, const int NN, const similarity::Space<dist_t>* space)
functions.description: Applies the HNSW heuristic 1 (relative neighborhood selection) to prune the candidate neighbor set stored in resultSet1 down to at most NN elements. It removes nodes that are closer to some already selected node than to the current node, promoting a diverse neighbor set.
requirements: space must be a valid pointer to the metric space used to compute distances between node data.
resultSet1 must contain candidate neighbors for this node with distances already computed between this->getData() and each neighbor’s data, consistent with space->IndexTimeDistance.
NN must be non-negative. If resultSet1.size() < NN the function returns without changes.
This method may be called under concurrent access; the caller should ensure external synchronization if needed for resultSet1.

functions.description: Applies HNSW heuristic 2 to prune the candidate neighbor set in resultSet1 to at most NN elements. Similar to heuristic 1 but with an adjusted selection loop; the level parameter is accepted but only used for logging/consistency in this implementation.
requirements: space must be a valid pointer to the metric space used to compute distances between node data.
resultSet1 must contain candidate neighbors for this node with distances computed between this->getData() and each neighbor’s data.
NN must be non-negative. If resultSet1.size() < NN the function returns without changes.

functions.name: similarity::HnswNode::getNeighborsByHeuristic3

void similarity::HnswNode::getNeighborsByHeuristic3(std::priority_queue<similarity::HnswNodeDistCloser<dist_t>>& resultSet1, const int NN, const similarity::Space<dist_t>* space, int level)
functions.description: Applies HNSW heuristic 3 to re-evaluate and prune neighbors. It first expands the candidate set by including neighbors of current candidates (at the specified level), re-scores them by distance to this node, and then selects a high-priority subset up to NN.
requirements: space must be a valid pointer to the metric space used to compute distances between node data.
level must be within [0, this->level] so that getAllFriends(level) is valid for all nodes considered.
resultSet1 initially contains candidate neighbors; function will pop and rebuild it, so the caller should not rely on its previous ordering after the call.
NN must be non-negative. If after expansion resultSet1.size() < NN, the function returns early.
The node’s adjacency lists must be initialized (init called).

functions.name: similarity::HnswNode::addFriendlevel
functions.signature:
template <typename dist_t>
void similarity::HnswNode::addFriendlevel(int level, similarity::HnswNode* element, const similarity::Space<dist_t>* space, int delaunay_type)
functions.description: Adds a bidirectional candidate neighbor (when used with link) to this node’s adjacency list at the given level and, if the list exceeds capacity, prunes it using either a Delaunay-like heuristic (types 1–3) or by removing the farthest neighbor (type 0).
requirements: Caller must ensure level is within [0, this->level] and allFriends_ is sized via init().
element must be a valid HnswNode pointer and must not already be present at this level; duplicates are silently ignored with an error message.
space must be valid and correspond to the metric used for distances; it is required for pruning when removing nodes.
delaunay_type must be one of: 0 (remove farthest), 1 (heuristic1), 2 (heuristic2), 3 (heuristic3).
This method acquires an internal mutex (accessGuard_) for this node; avoid deadlocks by not holding other node locks when calling.
Distance values used for pruning are computed between this->getData() and neighbors’ data using space->IndexTimeDistance.

functions.description: Computes the squared L2 distance between two float vectors using wide SIMD, processing only the largest multiple of 16 elements (intended for dimensions divisible by 16). Optimized for batch accumulation with an intermediate scratch buffer TmpRes used for SIMD horizontal reduction. Use when vector length is a multiple of 16 for best correctness/performance. Behavior is architecture-dependent: AVX and SSE2 store partial sums into TmpRes (alignment required); NEON reduces in-register; non-SIMD builds fall back to a scalar implementation.
requirements: pVect1 and pVect2 must be non-null and point to arrays of at least qty float elements.
qty should be a multiple of 16. Elements beyond floor(qty/16)*16 are not processed by this function.
TmpRes must be non-null and point to a buffer large enough for at least 8 floats (use the provided TMP_RES_ARRAY macro).

When compiled with AVX, TmpRes must be 32-byte aligned because _mm256_store_ps is used; with SSE2, TmpRes must be 16-byte aligned because _mm_store_ps is used. The TMP_RES_ARRAY macro provides correct alignment.
Inputs (pVect1/pVect2) need not be aligned (unaligned loads are used).
Function does not modify qty (despite being passed by reference).
Thread-safe as it has no global state and only reads inputs.

functions.description: Packs a sparse vector (list of id,value pairs) into a compact, block-structured byte buffer to accelerate overlap-based computations. On success, prBuff is set to a newly allocated buffer via new[]; the caller is responsible for deallocating it with delete[].

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: path string
# Requirements from stubs:
# - Used as std::string (FUZZ_PARAM_STR) and as filenames (FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME)
# - Should be valid, null-terminated when converted to C string
# - For filename use-cases, it should generally be writable/readable in the fuzzer temp dir.
# - For GetFileName, interesting cases include nested dirs, relative/absolute, extensions, trailing slashes, dots, unicode-ish bytes, long names up to ~255 per component.
# Strategy:
# - Produce a small container file that the harness can use for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME contents when it mirrors the provided buffer.
#   The harness is responsible for creating the file; our buffer just provides a plausible path string.
# - Generate a mix of absolute/relative paths, different separators, dot components, and extensions.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Random but seeded.

SEP_CHOICES = ["/", os.sep]
DRIVE_LETTERS = [chr(c) for c in range(ord('C'), ord('H'))]  # C..G
SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
EXTS = [".txt", ".bin", ".dat", ".sift", ".idx", ".log", ".gz", "", ".json"]

# Some components that trigger different code paths
SPECIAL_COMPONENTS = [
    ".", "..", "...", "~", "tmp", "var", "etc", "home", "usr", "bin",
    "con", "nul", "aux",  # interesting on Windows
]

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "μ", "ß", "ñ", "中", "文", "ф", "ø", "å", "é", "🙂"
]

RESERVED_ENDINGS = [" ", ".", "~"]  # components ending that may stress filename handling


def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 20) -> str:
    # Generate a single path component respecting typical max filename length (<=255)
    # Blend safe chars, digits, some unicode, and special tokens
    choice = rng.randint(0, 9)
    if choice == 0 and SPECIAL_COMPONENTS:
        base = rng.choice(SPECIAL_COMPONENTS)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(1, min(max_len, 32))
        base = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            base += rng.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS)
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            base += rng.choice(RESERVED_ENDINGS)
    # Ensure component length <= 255
    if len(base) > 255:
        base = base[:255]
    return base


def _rand_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    ext = rng.choice(EXTS)
    # Occasionally double extensions
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        ext += rng.choice([".bak", ".old", ".tmp"])  # still valid
    return ext


def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide absolute vs relative
    absolute = rng.random() < 0.5
    sep = rng.choice(SEP_CHOICES)

    parts: List[str] = []

    if os.name == 'nt':
        # Include Windows drive prefix occasionally
        if absolute and rng.random() < 0.8:
            drive = rng.choice(DRIVE_LETTERS)
            # Form like C:\ or C:/
            # We'll normalize to use chosen sep afterwards
            parts.append(f"{drive}:")
    else:
        if absolute:
            parts.append("")  # leading empty produces leading separator on join

    # Include 0..3 leading dot components to test normalization
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(rng.choice([".", ".."]))

    # Between 1 and 5 directories
    dir_qty = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(dir_qty):
        parts.append(_rand_component(rng, max_len=32))

    # Final filename
    filename = _rand_component(rng, max_len=64)
    # Add extension or not depending on content type
    filename += _rand_extension(rng)

    # Occasionally make it a directory (trailing separator); but many APIs expect files, so keep rare
    trailing_sep = rng.random() < 0.05

    parts.append(filename)

    # Join with chosen separator. For Windows drive like 'C:' ensure proper form
    if parts and parts[0].endswith(":"):
        # e.g., ["C:", "", "dir", "file.txt"] -> "C:\\dir\\file.txt"
        # If the next part is empty, it implies root; else relative to current dir on that drive
        left = parts[0]
        tail = parts[1:]
        path = left + sep + sep.join(tail) if (tail and tail[0] == "") else left + sep + sep.join(tail)
    else:
        path = sep.join(parts)

    if trailing_sep and not path.endswith(sep):
        path += sep

    # Cap total length to 4096 for safety
    if len(path) > 4000:
        path = path[:4000]

    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose from a set of scenarios to diversify across calls with same seed + different harness seeds
    scenario = rng.randint(0, 9)

    if scenario == 0:
        # Very short relative filename
        name = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))) + _rand_extension(rng)
        path = name
    elif scenario == 1:
        # Hidden file in current directory
        name = '.' + _rand_component(rng, max_len=20) + _rand_extension(rng)
        path = name
    elif scenario == 2:
        # Deep nested absolute
        path = _build_path(rng)
        if not (path.startswith('/') or (os.name == 'nt' and len(path) > 1 and path[1] == ':')):
            # Force absolute on POSIX
            path = '/' + path
    elif scenario == 3:
        # Path with spaces and unicode sprinkled
        comps = [
            _rand_component(rng, max_len=16) + (" " if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""),
            _rand_component(rng, max_len=16) + rng.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS),
            _rand_component(rng, max_len=16) + _rand_extension(rng)
        ]
        path = os.sep.join(comps)
    elif scenario == 4:
        # Use many dot components
        comps = [".", "..", ".", _rand_component(rng), _rand_component(rng) + _rand_extension(rng)]
        path = os.sep.join(comps)
    elif scenario == 5:
        # Long component near 255 chars
        comp_len = rng.randint(200, 255)
        longcomp = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(comp_len))
        path = os.sep + longcomp + os.sep + _rand_component(rng, max_len=64) + _rand_extension(rng)
    elif scenario == 6:
        # Mixed separators intentionally
        base = _build_path(rng)
        other_sep = '/' if os.sep != '/' else '\\'
        # Replace some separators to mix
        path = ''.join((other_sep if (ch == os.sep and rng.random() < 0.5) else ch) for ch in base)
    elif scenario == 7:
        # Trailing slash directory-like
        base = _build_path(rng)
        if not base.endswith(os.sep):
            base += os.sep
        path = base
    elif scenario == 8:
        # File with multiple extensions
        stem = _rand_component(rng, max_len=24)
        path = os.sep.join([
            _rand_component(rng, max_len=12),
            stem + ".tar.gz"
        ])
    else:
        # Default general case
        path = _build_path(rng)

    # Ensure not empty and reasonable length
    if not path:
        path = "file.dat"
    if len(path) > 4096:
        path = path[:4096]

    # Return as bytes; C++ side will treat std::string and c_str() as null-terminated
    return path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

def _rand_filename_component(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    # Safe filename characters
    alphabet = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_.'
    n = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _sift_line(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Optional label prefix: label=<int> <space>
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        label = rng.randint(-1000, 1000)
        parts.append(f"label={label} ")
    # 128 uint8 values [0..255], space-separated
    vals = [str(rng.randint(0,255)) for _ in range(128)]
    parts.append(' '.join(vals))
    line = ''.join(parts) + "\n"
    return line.encode('utf-8')

def _sift_text_file(rng: random.Random, lines: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a text file compatible with SpaceL2SqrSift reader (typical format: optional label=, then 128 numbers)
    buf = bytearray()
    for _ in range(lines):
        buf += _sift_line(rng)
    return bytes(buf)

def _bin_string_with_len_prefix(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    # [uint32_t len][len bytes]
    length = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    payload = rng.randbytes(length) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))
    return struct.pack('<I', length) + payload

def _sparse_bin_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Craft a plausible header for SpaceSparse*BinFast readers.
    # Many NMSLIB binary formats start with a magic + simple header. We'll create a small, consistent header:
    # magic(4) = b'SPBF', version(1), flags(1), reserved(2), count(uint32), dim(uint32)
    magic = b'SPBF'
    version = bytes([rng.randint(0, 2)])
    flags = bytes([rng.randint(0, 3)])
    reserved = b"\x00\x00"
    count = rng.randint(0, 16)
    dim = rng.randint(1, 256)
    return magic + version + flags + reserved + struct.pack('<II', count, dim)

def _sparse_bin_vector(rng: random.Random, dim: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a sparse vector as: nnz(uint32), then nnz entries of (index(uint32), value(float32))
    nnz = rng.randint(0, min(dim, 32))
    # Ensure unique sorted indices within [0, dim-1]
    idxs = sorted(rng.sample(range(dim), nnz)) if nnz > 0 else []
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += struct.pack('<I', nnz)
    for i in idxs:
        val = rng.uniform(-5.0, 5.0)
        buf += struct.pack('<If', i, val)
    return bytes(buf)

def _sparse_bin_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate header + a few vectors
    dim = rng.randint(8, 256)
    header = b'SPBF' + bytes([1, 0]) + b"\x00\x00" + struct.pack('<II', rng.randint(1, 8), dim)
    vec_qty = rng.randint(1, 8)
    buf = bytearray(header)
    for _ in range(vec_qty):
        buf += _sparse_bin_vector(rng, dim)
    return bytes(buf)

def _bitvector_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Simple bitvector representation often used: first uint32 = length in bits, followed by bytes
    bits = rng.randint(1, 2048)
    bytelen = (bits + 7) // 8
    payload = rng.randbytes(bytelen) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(bytelen))
    return struct.pack('<I', bits) + payload

def _logger_weight_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Weight file for SpaceSparseDenseFusion: craft a small textual config with components/weights
    # Not strictly specified, but provide reasonable key=value lines that parsers may accept.
    lines = []
    comp_qty = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(comp_qty):
        w_idx = rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0)
        w_qry = rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0)
        # component i description text
        lines.append(f"component{i}=sparse")
        lines.append(f"w_index{i}={w_idx:.6f}")
        lines.append(f"w_query{i}={w_qry:.6f}")
    return ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n').encode('utf-8')

def _maybe_prefix_label_line(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # For StringSpace/Levenshtein readers, a simple text line
    # Optionally prefix with label= as Object::extractLabel understands
    s = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s += f"label={rng.randint(-5,5)} "
    length = rng.randint(0, 64)
    alphabet = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz '
    s += ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return (s + '\n').encode('utf-8')

def _compose_multi_section_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a file that may satisfy multiple consumers: start with a valid binary string id,
    # then append a SIFT-friendly text block, then a sparse binary block.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    parts.append(_bin_string_with_len_prefix(rng, max_len=64))
    # Separator comments/newlines (ignored by binary readers, useful for text ones if positioned later)
    parts.append(b"# SIFT block\n")
    lines = rng.randint(1, 8)
    parts.append(_sift_text_file(rng, lines))
    # Append a sparse block
    parts.append(_sparse_bin_file(rng))
    # Ensure size limit
    out = b''.join(parts)
    return out[:4096]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose one of several formats tailored to the fuzzer stubs that read filenames with arbitrary content.
    choice = rng.randint(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        return _sift_text_file(rng, lines=rng.randint(1, 20))[:4096]
    elif choice == 1:
        return _bin_string_with_len_prefix(rng, max_len=256)[:4096]
    elif choice == 2:
        return _sparse_bin_file(rng)[:4096]
    elif choice == 3:
        return _bitvector_file(rng)[:4096]
    elif choice == 4:
        # Logger weight/config style
        return _logger_weight_file(rng)[:4096]
    elif choice == 5:
        # Simple string lines, suitable for Levenshtein readers
        buf = bytearray()
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 32)):
            buf += _maybe_prefix_label_line(rng)
        return bytes(buf)[:4096]
    else:
        return _compose_multi_section_file(rng)[:4096]

import random
import struct

# This generator focuses on producing valid, useful bytes for fuzz stubs that
# consume FUZZ_PARAM(int/unsigned), FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), and filenames. It crafts
# structured content: pools of signed/unsigned 32-bit integers and a set of
# varied strings, including SIFT-like lines and label-prefixed lines that align
# with Object::extractLabel expectations.

MAX_SIZE = 4096
LABEL_PREFIX = "__label__"


def _pack_u32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _to_i32_range(v: int) -> int:
    # Convert arbitrary int to signed 32-bit range [-2^31, 2^31-1]
    v &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    if v >= 0x80000000:
        v -= 0x100000000
    return v


def _pack_i32(v: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<i', _to_i32_range(v))


def sift_line_from_bytes(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a canonical 128-dim SIFT uint8 vector as space-separated decimals.
    vals = [str(rnd.randrange(0, 256)) for _ in range(128)]
    return " ".join(vals)


def random_ascii(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = [chr(c) for c in range(32, 127)]
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def random_utf8(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rnd.random()
        if t < 0.75:
            out.append(chr(rnd.randint(32, 126)))
        elif t < 0.9:
            out.append(chr(rnd.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF)))
        else:
            out.append(chr(rnd.randint(0x0800, 0xFFFF)))
    return ''.join(out)


def label_line(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    lbl = _to_i32_range(rnd.getrandbits(32))
    body = random_utf8(rnd, 0, 40)
    return f"{LABEL_PREFIX}{lbl} {body}"


def craft_strings(rnd: random.Random):
    strs = []
    strs.append("")
    strs.append("a")
    strs.append(random_ascii(rnd, 3, 12))
    strs.append(random_utf8(rnd, 10, 40))
    strs.append(random_utf8(rnd, 50, 120))
    strs.append(label_line(rnd))
    strs.append(sift_line_from_bytes(rnd))
    strs.append(random_utf8(rnd, 200, 400))
    return strs


def craft_ints(rnd: random.Random):
    ints = [
        0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, 7, -7, 10, -10,
        1024, -1024, 2**31 - 1, -2**31,
        _to_i32_range(rnd.getrandbits(32)),
        _to_i32_range(rnd.getrandbits(32)),
        _to_i32_range(rnd.getrandbits(32)),
    ]
    uints = [
        0, 1, 33, 64, 127, 255, 1000, 100000, 2**32 - 1,
        rnd.randrange(0, 2**32), rnd.randrange(0, 2**32),
    ]
    return ints, uints


def encode_len_prefixed(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]
    return _pack_u32(len(b)) + b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    parts = []
    parts.append(b'NMGEN\x00')

    # Provide a join character candidate directly in bytes to influence modulo logic
    join_char = rnd.randint(33, 96)
    parts.append(_pack_u32(join_char))

    sints, uints = craft_ints(rnd)

    parts.append(_pack_u32(len(sints)))
    for v in sints:
        parts.append(_pack_i32(v))

    parts.append(_pack_u32(len(uints)))
    for v in uints:
        parts.append(_pack_u32(v))

    strings = craft_strings(rnd)
    for lbl in [0, 1, -1, 123456, -987654321]:
        base = random_utf8(rnd, 0, 30)
        strings.append(f"{LABEL_PREFIX}{_to_i32_range(lbl)} {base}")

    parts.append(_pack_u32(len(strings)))
    for s in strings:
        parts.append(encode_len_prefixed(s))

    blob = b''.join(parts)
    if len(blob) > MAX_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:MAX_SIZE]
    return blob

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator focuses on producing valid and interesting arbitrary binary blobs
# to drive the fuzzer stubs:
# - similarity::Object::Object (expects payload of arbitrary bytes, header composed by stub)
# - SIFT-related spaces expect exactly 128 bytes payload in Objects
# - Vector distance functions expect buffers that can be interpreted as float arrays
# - Writers expect reasonable-sized payloads
# We therefore generate payloads of varying sizes, with patterns that are likely to
# exercise different numeric behaviors when interpreted as floats, while always being valid bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Common float bit patterns to trigger edge behaviors when interpreted as float
SPECIAL_FLOAT_PATTERNS = [
    0x00000000,  # +0.0
    0x80000000,  # -0.0
    0x3f800000,  # 1.0
    0xbf800000,  # -1.0
    0x7f800000,  # +inf
    0xff800000,  # -inf
    0x7fc00000,  # NaN (quiet)
    0x00800000,  # smallest normal
    0x00000001,  # smallest subnormal
    0x3f000000,  # 0.5
    0x40000000,  # 2.0
    0x40490fdb,  # pi ~3.1415927
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_patterns(rng: random.Random, qty: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate a sequence of 32-bit values mixing special patterns and random floats
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(qty):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            val = rng.choice(SPECIAL_FLOAT_PATTERNS)
        else:
            # random 32-bit pattern, but bias towards reasonable finite magnitudes
            # by constructing from a random float range and packing
            f = rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0)
            val = struct.unpack('<I', struct.pack('<f', f))[0]
        out += struct.pack('<I', val)
    return bytes(out)


def _sift_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Exactly 128 bytes as expected by SIFT-based spaces
    # Compose from uint8-like values; include gradients and random chunks
    payload = bytearray(128)
    # gradient
    for i in range(128):
        payload[i] = (i * 2) % 256
    # Overwrite random windows with random bytes for diversity
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        start = rng.randrange(0, 128)
        length = rng.randrange(1, 16)
        end = min(128, start + length)
        payload[start:end] = _rand_bytes(rng, end - start)
    return bytes(payload)


def _float_vector_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create two back-to-back float arrays a|b with same length so that
    # consumers can read them as two vectors.
    # Choose a length that keeps total size modest.
    length = rng.randint(1, 256)
    # Create a mix of special and regular floats
    block = _mix_patterns(rng, length) + _mix_patterns(rng, length)
    return block


def _small_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Small random payload used for general Object data
    size = rng.randint(0, 512)
    # Combine random bytes and some ASCII text fragments
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # ASCII fragment with possible label prefix seen by code elsewhere
    ascii_fragments = [
        b"label:0 ", b"label:1 ", b"",
        b"The quick brown fox ", b"SIFT\x00\x01\x02",
    ]
    parts.append(rng.choice(ascii_fragments))
    parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, max(0, size - sum(len(p) for p in parts))))
    return b"".join(parts)[:size]


def _binary_sparse_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a compact binary-like blob to serve as plausible sparse-binary writer input
    # Not adhering to a specific format, just bounded random data
    size = rng.randint(8, 256)
    return _rand_bytes(rng, size)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a scenario to cover different stubs usage patterns
    # 0: SIFT 128-byte payload
    # 1: Two float vectors back-to-back
    # 2: Small arbitrary payload
    # 3: Mixed block: header-ish then payload
    # 4: Sparse-binary-like payload
    choice = rng.randrange(5)

    if choice == 0:
        data = _sift_payload(rng)
    elif choice == 1:
        data = _float_vector_block(rng)
    elif choice == 2:
        data = _small_payload(rng)
    elif choice == 3:
        # Create a buffer with a small header-like preface followed by content
        # Header: 4 bytes id, 4 bytes label, 8 bytes length (little endian)
        # Then payload of that length (not required by stubs, but valid bytes)
        payload = _small_payload(rng)
        id_val = rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
        label_val = rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1)
        header = struct.pack('<i', id_val) + struct.pack('<i', label_val) + struct.pack('<Q', len(payload))
        data = header + payload
    else:
        data = _binary_sparse_like(rng)

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]

    # Avoid returning empty buffers too often; if empty, add a byte
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"

    return data
